review_notes: Read the whole file and the definitions of nsmulPt (Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_QMModuli.lean) and RelativeGroupLaw.nsmul (Definitions/Def_GoodReductionJacobian_RelativeGroupLawKernel.lean). Both are project-internal, not Mathlib. I found no Mathlib concept this file duplicates; FactorsThrough, pushPt and the others are specific to this project. The one finding is a competing pair of project definitions, and this file only supplies the bridge lemma between them, so it is weaker evidence. I did not check how widely each version is used, or whether universe constraints (Scheme.{u} versus Scheme.{0}) are a reason to keep both. The other nsmulPt copies elsewhere are in files I did not read.

findings.excerpt: L.nsmul t n x = nsmulPt L t n x
findings.problem: The project defines the same specific concept, iterated group-law multiplication by a natural number on SchemeHomOver points, twice. `RelativeGroupLaw.nsmul` is defined by Nat.rec with `G.one t` and `G.mul t ih x`. `nsmulPt` is defined by structural recursion with the same base and step. This file has to prove they are equal, and `nsmulPt_val` then goes back through `nsmul_natural`. Further `nsmulPt` definitions appear in other files (e.g. S_GoodReductionJacobian_RelativeGroupLaw_exists_hom_comp_eq_comp_schemeNsmul_comp_of_natCast_eq_zero.lean and S_ModularCurve_XOneP_eq_zero_...), so the duplication recurs. Lemmas stated for one version do not apply to the other without a conversion like this.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `nsmulPt`, or make it a reducible alias of `RelativeGroupLaw.nsmul`. Then `nsmul_eq_nsmulPt` becomes unnecessary. Rewrite `nsmulPt_val` and `nsmulPt_eq_one_of_factorsThrough` in terms of `L.nsmul`, which already has the simp lemmas `nsmul_zero` and `nsmul_succ` and the lemma `nsmul_natural`. Remove the `Scheme.{0}` copies in other files in the same way.
findings.benefit: There is one API for repeated multiplication of points. Readers no longer need to know which of the two versions a lemma uses. Bridge lemmas like this one disappear, and the existing `nsmul_*` lemmas can be used directly.

evidence.excerpt: | n + 1, P => L.mul t (nsmulPt L t n P) P
Nat.rec (G.one t) (fun _ ih => G.mul t ih x) n
